title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are grappling with a mix of resilience strategies and technological advancements this week. From satellite network recovery plans to the ongoing challenges in missile production, the landscape remains as complex as ever.

themes.title: Satellite Network Resilience
themes.body: DARPA's new initiative to rapidly rebuild satellite networks post-attack underscores the increasing vulnerability of space assets. As geopolitical tensions rise, the emphasis on resilience could reshape funding and priorities in the sector.

themes.title: Missile Production Challenges
themes.body: A bottleneck in solid rocket motor production is complicating the push for increased missile output. This could delay defense readiness as manufacturers struggle to meet rising demands.

themes.title: Lunar Landers Take Shape
themes.body: Revised plans for the Artemis lunar lander reflect ongoing adjustments in NASA's ambitious lunar return strategy. As timelines shift, the focus on sustainable exploration becomes ever more pressing.

themes.title: Funding for Space Initiatives
themes.body: The recent $1.4 billion boost to the space resilience line in the FY27 budget signals a commitment to enhancing national security in space. This funding could catalyze new projects aimed at countering emerging threats.
